declarations.checkedType: agent(token: string of private) -> record[string of private]
declarations.documentation:
The `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header every Google API call carries. @token@ is a
`string of private` (a runtime-resolved credential); concatenation propagates the taint and the header
record is a private-capable submission sink, so the secret leaves only toward Google's server — never into
a URL, a log or a trace.
declarations.name: bearer
declarations.signature: agent bearer(token: string of private) -> record[string of private]

declarations.checkedType: agent(body: string, context: string, status: integer) -> (api_error | auth_error)
declarations.documentation:
Classify a failed Google API response into `http.api_failure` — `http.classify_status` under the name
the Google packages already spell. A 401 or 403 is `http.auth_error` (Google rejected the resolved access
token — revoked, or scoped too narrowly — which a replay converter turns into a fresh token resolution,
and, when the credential is refresh-dead, the runtime's re-authorization park); every other non-2xx is
`http.api_error`. The failing @status@ RIDES on whichever comes out, so a caller decides transient
(408 / 429 / 5xx) versus refusal by comparing a number.

403 IS READ AS AUTH even though Google also returns it for quota exhaustion, and that reading is now the
STDLIB's rather than this package's: a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again, costing one wasted
retry, where reading a revoked token as a quota problem costs the recovery entirely. The asymmetry held for
every authenticated REST API, not only Google's, which is why the argument moved to where every package can
inherit it.

@context@ names the call ("list_events", "send", "watch") and @body@ is the response's own,
carried through VERBATIM as the error's `message` — the two halves stay apart so a renderer shows either
alone and Google's diagnosis is never edited to make room for a prefix.
declarations.name: classify_api_error

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

declarations.checkedType: agent(body: unknown, context: string, method: string, token: string of private, url: string) -> unknown with throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Issue an authenticated Google API call — @method@ to @url@ carrying @body@ and the `Bearer` @token@ —
and return the reply parsed as JSON. THE one place the header, the 2xx test and the failure classification
live, for every Google package and every verb: `google_get` is this agent with the method fixed, and every
write in `gmail` and `google_calendar` is one call to it.

@body@ is the request document as a value tree (a record / array / scalar), sent as application/json, or
`null` for a call that carries no document — every GET, and a DELETE. Both cases are absorbed here rather
than at the six call sites that used to spell them.

A 2xx WITH AN EMPTY BODY answers `null`. That is what a 204 No Content always is (`events.delete`), and
what any 2xx Google chose to answer without a document is; a caller that wanted one reads `null` and says
so, instead of meeting a `json.parse_error` for a reply that was never malformed. A 2xx body that is not
JSON does throw `json.parse_error` — an API that broke its promise.

A NON-2XX throws `classify_api_error(@context@, ...)`: 401/403 → `http.auth_error`, every other status →
`http.api_error`, each carrying the status, @context@ and Google's own body.

@token@ is passed IN rather than asked for: the `credential` request belongs to the package the call is
made from (`gmail.credential`, `google_calendar.credential`), so the caller writes
`call(..., token = credential())` and this agent stays free of any capability of its own.

declarations.checkedType: agent(context: string, token: string of private, url: string) -> unknown with throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Issue an authenticated GET to a Google API @url@ with @token@ and return its parsed JSON body — `call`
with the method fixed to "GET" and no request document, so a read's call site spells neither. The
`Bearer` header, the 2xx check and the error classification are `call`'s; @context@ names the calling
agent for the failure's message. A non-2xx becomes `classify_api_error(@context@, ...)` (401/403 →
`http.auth_error`, else `http.api_error`); a 2xx body that is not JSON throws `json.parse_error`.
